questions_and_answers.question_text: What is the preferred word order with a modifying phrase?
Where else may nèige or zhèige be placed?
Why is the preferred order better in longer phrases?
Where is the adverb zhèng placed?
Which expression is more colloquial than zhèng shi?
Write the Chinese for "That's him all right!"
Write the Chinese for "That's precisely why he left."

answers.answer_text: Zhèng shi yīnwei zhèige, tā cái zǒu le.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "This is just the book I want to read."

answers.answer_text: Wǒ yào kànde zhèng shi zhèiběn shū.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Give the alternative to Zhèng shi tā!

articles.text:
5. A: Zài nàr xiě zìde nèige rén     Is that person writing over there her
      shi bu shi tā zhàngfu?         husband?
   B: Zhèng shi tā!                  That's him all right!

Notes on No. 5

zài nàr xiě zìde nèige rén: "the person writing over there." Notice once again that the PREFERRED word order is to put the SPECIFIER-NUMBER-COUNTER BETWEEN the modifying phrase and the noun.

Modifying phrase | Specifier-Number-Counter | Noun
hěn hǎo kànde    | nèi sān ge               | nǚháir

It is ALSO possible to put the nèige or zhèige at the HEAD of the phrase (nèige xiě zìde rén), but especially in LONGER phrases it sounds better to keep nèige or zhèige CLOSE TO THE NOUN.

zhèng: "just, right, exactly, precisely." Like other adverbs, zhèng is placed in FRONT of a verb.

Wǒ zhèng yào zhǎo ni shāngliang  I was just looking for you to talk
zhèijiàn shìqing.                about this matter.
Nǐ chuān zhèige yánsè zhèng      This color is just right for you.
héshì.
Wǒ yào kànde zhèng shi zhèiběn   This is just the book I want to read.
shū.
Zhèng shi yīnwei zhèige, tā cái  That's precisely why he left.
zǒu le.

Jiù shi is MORE COLLOQUIAL than zhèng shi. For 5B, you could also say Jiù shi tā!
